example.ja: 昨日遅くまで起きてて、眠い。
example.english: I stayed up late last night, so I'm sleepy.

examplePolite.romaji: Kinou osoku made okite ita node, nemui desu.
examplePolite.ja: 昨日遅くまで起きていたので、眠いです。
examplePolite.english: I stayed up late last night, so I'm sleepy.

notes: Tsukareta is worn out from effort; nemui only means you want to sleep.

use: Covers both something disgusting and your own nausea: on its own, 'kimochi warui' often means 'I feel sick'.

example.ja: 飲みすぎて気持ち悪い。
example.english: I drank too much, I feel sick.

examplePolite.ja: 飲みすぎて気持ち悪いです。
examplePolite.english: I drank too much, I feel sick.

notes: Slang short form kimoi is rude when aimed at a person. Opposite: kimochi ii.

use: For physical comfort: a breeze, a hot bath, a massage, a good stretch.

examplePolite.romaji: Kaze ga kimochi ii desu ne.
examplePolite.ja: 風が気持ちいいですね。

notes: Past is kimochi yokatta, not kimochi iikatta.

use: Your body feels heavy and slow, often before a cold or after bad sleep.

example.english: My body feels kind of heavy.

examplePolite.ja: ちょっと体がだるいです。

notes: Young people also use it like mendokusai: gakkou darui = school is such a drag.

example.ja: 蚊に刺されて、すごくかゆい。
example.english: A mosquito bit me and it's really itchy.

examplePolite.romaji: Ka ni sasarete, totemo kayui desu.
examplePolite.ja: 蚊に刺されて、とてもかゆいです。
examplePolite.english: A mosquito bit me and it's really itchy.

notes: Kaku = to scratch: kakanaide = don't scratch it.

use: Praise for looks (often men), clothes, cars, or a cool thing someone did.

example.ja: そのジャケット、かっこいいね。

examplePolite.ja: そのジャケット、かっこいいですね。

notes: Past is kakkoyokatta. Opposite: kakkowarui = uncool, embarrassing. Also written カッコいい.

use: Often a compliment on looking young: 'wakai ne!' = you look so young!

example.ja: お母さん、すごく若いね！

examplePolite.ja: お母さん、とても若いですね。

notes: Wakai koro = when I was young. Wakaku mieru = look young.

use: For people, clothes and places: 'oshare na kafe' = a trendy café.

example.romaji: Kyou no fuku, oshare da ne.
example.ja: 今日の服、おしゃれだね。

examplePolite.romaji: Kyou no fuku, oshare desu ne.
examplePolite.ja: 今日の服、おしゃれですね。

notes: Oshare suru = dress up. Kakkoii is cool; oshare is fashionable.

use: Mostly about couples: 'oniai da ne' = you two are perfect together.

example.romaji: Futari, honto ni oniai da ne.
example.ja: 二人、ほんとにお似合いだね。
example.english: You two make a really great couple.

examplePolite.romaji: Ofutari, hontou ni oniai desu ne.
examplePolite.ja: お二人、本当にお似合いですね。
examplePolite.english: You two make a really great couple.

notes: For clothes the verb niau is more common: niatteru = it suits you.

english: what a pain; such a hassle; can't be bothered
use: The everyday grumble about chores; of a person, 'mendokusai hito' = a difficult, high-maintenance person.

example.ja: 料理するの、めんどくさいな。

examplePolite.romaji: Ryouri suru no wa mendokusai desu ne.
examplePolite.ja: 料理するのはめんどくさいですね。
examplePolite.english: Cooking is such a hassle, isn't it?

notes: Spoken form of mendoukusai; often cut further to mendoi. The noun mendou (hassle) sounds softer in polite talk.

use: For things that hurt or wear you down: a breakup, a hard job, getting up early.

example.romaji: Asa hayaku okiru no, tsurai na.
example.ja: 朝早く起きるの、つらいな。

examplePolite.romaji: Asa hayaku okiru no wa tsurai desu.
examplePolite.ja: 朝早く起きるのはつらいです。
examplePolite.english: Getting up early is hard for me.

notes: The kanji 辛い is also read karai (spicy); in speech the meaning is clear.

use: For anything demanding: a hard workout, a packed schedule, tight shoes.

example.ja: この仕事、けっこうきついよ。

examplePolite.romaji: Kono shigoto wa kekkou kitsui desu.
examplePolite.ja: この仕事はけっこうきついです。

notes: Zubon ga kitsui = my trousers are tight. Kitsui iikata = a harsh way of putting it.

use: Covers both a draining task and how drained you feel: 'kyou shindoi' = I'm wiped today.

example.ja: 今日は残業でしんどかった。
example.english: Today was exhausting with all the overtime.

examplePolite.romaji: Kyou wa zangyou de shindokatta desu.
examplePolite.ja: 今日は残業でしんどかったです。
examplePolite.english: Today was exhausting with all the overtime.

notes: Started in Kansai, now used everywhere. Close to tsurai and kitsui, but more about fatigue.

english: painful; hard to breathe; hard to bear
use: Strain you are struggling under: a tight chest, being too full, money trouble.

example.ja: 食べすぎてお腹が苦しい。
example.english: I ate too much, I'm painfully full.

examplePolite.ja: 食べすぎてお腹が苦しいです。
examplePolite.english: I ate too much, I'm painfully full.

notes: Tsurai is emotional hardship; kurushii leans physical. Kurushii iiwake = a lame excuse.

english: lonely; sad to be apart; (a place) empty
use: Also how you say you'll miss someone: 'sabishiku naru ne' = I'll miss you.

example.ja: みんな帰っちゃうと寂しいな。
example.english: It's lonely when everyone goes home.

examplePolite.romaji: Minna ga kaeru to sabishii desu ne.
examplePolite.ja: みんなが帰ると寂しいですね。
examplePolite.english: It's lonely when everyone goes home.

example.ja: その映画、悲しすぎて泣いた。
example.english: That movie was so sad I cried.

examplePolite.ja: その映画は悲しすぎて泣きました。
examplePolite.english: That movie was so sad I cried.

notes: Sabishii is lonely or missing someone; kanashii is sad about something that happened.

english: poor thing; pitiful; that's sad (for them)
use: Feeling sorry for a person or animal: 'kawaisou!' = oh, poor thing!

example.romaji: Kono neko, ame de nurete kawaisou.
example.ja: この猫、雨で濡れてかわいそう。
example.english: This poor cat is soaked from the rain.

examplePolite.romaji: Kono neko, ame de nurete kawaisou desu ne.
examplePolite.ja: この猫、雨で濡れてかわいそうですね。
examplePolite.english: This poor cat is soaked from the rain.

notes: Sounds like kawaii + sou, but it only means pity, never 'looks cute'.

use: Said the moment something from the past comes back: an old song, a photo, an old friend.

example.ja: うわ、この写真懐かしい！
example.english: Wow, this photo takes me back!

examplePolite.ja: この写真、懐かしいですね。
examplePolite.english: This photo really takes me back.

notes: A warm, happy feeling, not a sad one.
